problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the vertical asymptotes of the function  $f(x)=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\pi x)?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a General Expression for the Asymptotes of a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function
examples.problem: What expression gives all of the vertical asymptotes of the function  $f(x)=\tan\left(2x\right)?$
examples.worked_solution:
The asymptotes of $y=\tan x$ are given by the expression

$$
x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n \pi,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the asymptotes of $\tan\left(2x\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $2x.$ This gives

$$
2x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi.
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{n\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the expression giving all the vertical asymptotes is $x= \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{n\pi}{2},$ where $n$ is an integer.

feedback.problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the zeros of the function $f(x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{3})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
feedback.worked_solution:
The zeros of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ are given by

$$
x=n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the zeros of $f(x)=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{3}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{3}).$ This gives

$$
\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{3}=n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{3} & =n\pi  \\ \frac{x}{4} & =n\pi +\frac{\pi }{3} \\ x & =4n\pi +\frac{4\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the zeros are $x=\frac{4\pi }{3}+4n\pi ,$ where $n$ is an integer.
